name: nimblescape-devspaces-2
description: Open your GitHub repositories in dev containers on your own Docker. Uses your GitHub sign-in (scopes repo and read:org), runs Docker and the Dev Containers CLI, can install Docker after you confirm, and runs a background container that updates images, the VS Code Server and extensions. Before your first devspace, it does not contact the Docker engine. The background container keeps running only on a remote Docker host, and a command removes it.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode, Devspaces uses only your user settings: the values of its settings in the workspace or folder are ignored.

devspaces-monitor-off.description: Devspaces: a stopped devspace, the local Docker, and Open devspace… (a monitor switched off).

devspaces-monitor-on.description: Devspaces: a devspace that another window uses (a monitor switched on).

devspaces-monitor-connected.description: Devspaces: the devspace of this window (a monitor switched on, with the connection sign).

devspaces-monitor-remote.description: Devspaces: a remote Docker host (a monitor switched off, with the connection sign).

devspaces-monitor-running.description: Devspaces: a devspace whose container runs without a window (a monitor switched off, with the play sign).

devspaces-monitor-updating.description: Devspaces: a devspace that is being updated, rebuilt or deleted (a monitor switched off, with the clock sign).

devspaces-monitor-no-container.description: Devspaces: a devspace whose container is missing (a monitor switched off, with the ring sign).

devspaces-monitor-warning.description: Devspaces: a devspace whose workspace volume is missing, or a Docker endpoint that is not supported (a monitor switched off, with the warning sign).

colors.description: Devspaces: the name, the description and the icon of a row without an active devspace (view Devspaces) and of an object of Devspaces that is not active (view Docker Hosts).

Devspaces: the name, the description and the icon of an active object that is not of Devspaces in the view Docker Hosts (a running container, or an image, a volume or a network that a running container uses).
Devspaces: the name, the description and the icon of an inactive object that is not of Devspaces in the view Docker Hosts.

viewsWelcome.contents: Devspaces runs your devspaces in its own VM with Docker Engine, which is not set up yet. It does not use Docker Desktop or Docker Engine of this computer.

1. Install WSL 2, which the VM of Devspaces needs on Windows. Windows asks for administrator permission; restart Windows afterwards, and Devspaces goes on with step 2 by itself.
[Install WSL 2](command:devspaces.dockerSetup.installWsl)

2. Set up Docker for Devspaces: Devspaces creates its own WSL distribution (its VM) with Docker Engine, downloads its Docker CLI and connects to the distribution, without Docker Desktop and without administrator permission. When WSL 2 is missing, it installs WSL 2 first, and goes on after the restart of Windows. The log names the downloads and the folder.
[Set Up Docker for Devspaces](command:devspaces.setUpWslDistribution)

Set up Docker for Devspaces: Devspaces downloads Lima and the disk of its own VM with Docker Engine, creates the VM, downloads its Docker CLI and connects to the VM, without Docker Desktop and without administrator permission. The log names the downloads and the folder.
[Set Up Docker for Devspaces](command:devspaces.setUpLimaVm)

Set up Docker for Devspaces: Devspaces downloads Lima and the disk of its own VM with Docker Engine, creates the VM, downloads its Docker CLI and connects to the VM, without administrator permission. Without QEMU, Devspaces first installs it in a terminal, where sudo asks for your password. The log names the downloads and the folder.
[Set Up Docker for Devspaces](command:devspaces.setUpLimaVm)
Your repositories appear here once the VM is set up. Devspaces starts the VM when needed, and the VM powers itself off when nothing runs there.

Or use Docker on another computer that you reach over SSH, without Docker on this computer. Devspaces downloads the Docker CLI that it needs into its own folder; this needs no administrator permission.
[Use a Remote Docker Host…](command:devspaces.useRemoteDockerHost)

Sign in with GitHub to see your repositories that have a Dev Container configuration.
Devspaces asks for the scopes repo (read and change the repositories that you can access, also the private ones) and read:org (read your organization memberships). It works only with accounts on github.com.
[Sign in with GitHub](command:devspaces.signIn)
Your VS Code is set up for GitHub Enterprise Server or GHE.com. Devspaces cannot use an account there. Sign in with an account on github.com.

No repository with a Dev Container configuration was found.
[Refresh](command:devspaces.refresh)

You have no devspace on this Docker engine yet.
[Show All Repositories](command:devspaces.showAllRepositories)

The repository list could not be loaded. Check the internet connection and try again.
[Refresh](command:devspaces.refresh)
[Show Log](command:devspaces.showLog)

devspaces.reopenLastOnStartup.markdownDescription: When VS Code starts with an empty window, open the devspace of the window that you closed last, if that window was connected to a devspace and you did not stop the devspace with **Stop**.

devspaces.openInNewWindow.markdownDescription:
Where **Start** opens a devspace.

- On: in a new window; the current window keeps its devspace (an empty window is used directly)
- Off: in the current window

The context menu always offers the other choice. A devspace that is already open in a window is never opened twice: that window comes to the front.

devspaces.defaultImage.markdownDescription:
An image, for example `ghcr.io/majikmate/devcontainer-base:latest`, that a devspace can start from. A repository with a Dev Container configuration gets a `default` row, its own devspace; one without is listed too and starts from the image. Empty: no default image; only repositories with a configuration are listed.

[Default image in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#default-image)

devspaces.startWithDefaultImage.markdownDescription:
Only with **Default Image** set: the place of the `default` row among the child rows of a repository, and what a double-click on the repository starts.

- On: the `default` row comes first, before the rows of the configurations, and a double-click on the repository starts the default image
- Off: the `default` row comes last, and a double-click on the repository starts its first configuration

Every row keeps its own **Start**.

devspaces.stopOnClose.markdownDescription:
Stop a devspace's container 5 minutes after its last window closes (enough for a window reload).

- Off: every devspace keeps running until you stop it
- To keep only some running, use **Keep Running When Closed** on their rows

devspaces.stopAfterMinutes.markdownDescription:
Minutes without any sign from a window before the Monitor stops the container anyway.

Covers the cases where the window cannot say goodbye: this computer sleeps or goes offline, or VS Code crashes. Devspaces that keep running when closed are never stopped.

devspaces.cacheUpdateSchedule.patternErrorMessage: An interval in whole minutes from 60 (an hour) to 1440 (a day), for example 120, or a cron schedule of five fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) with at least 60 minutes between two of its times, for example 7 6 * * * (every day at 06:07).
devspaces.cacheUpdateSchedule.markdownDescription:
When the Monitor on each Docker engine updates the images, the VS Code server and the extensions of your devspaces: a cron expression in your time zone, with at least 60 minutes between two of its times, for example `7 6 * * *` (daily at 06:07, the default), or the minutes between two runs (60 to 1440).

[The background run in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#the-background-run)

devspaces.stopMonitorWhenIdle.markdownDescription:
End the Monitor container on a remote Docker host when no devspace has run there for 5 minutes; the next start starts it again. Off: it keeps running there. On the WSL distribution or VM of Devspaces and on the Docker of this computer, the Monitor always ends when idle, whatever this says.

[The background run in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#the-background-run)

devspaces.updateImagesOnConnect.markdownDescription:
At each open, check whether the devspace's base image or Features have a newer version, and if so update the devspace (your files are kept).

Off: the devspace keeps its image until you choose **Rebuild**.

devspaces.updateContainer.markdownDescription:
What a start does when a newer image is available for the existing container of a devspace. The update creates the container again; your files in the workspace are kept.

[The update at a start in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#the-update-at-a-start)
enumDescriptions: Update the container without a dialog. A running container is stopped and created again.
Say that the container is updated now, with Continue or Cancel. Cancel leaves the devspace closed.
Ask first, with Update Now or Later. Later opens the current container without the update.

devspaces.respectShutdownActionNone.markdownDescription:
Keep a devspace running after its window closes when its `devcontainer.json` says `"shutdownAction": "none"`.

Off (default): that line is ignored and **Stop On Close** applies.

devspaces.owners.markdownDescription:
Organizations or accounts whose repositories the sidebar lists.

- Empty: all repositories you can access
- Or use **Select Organizations…** (filter icon of the sidebar)

Example: `["majikmate", "acme"]`

devspaces.includeArchived.markdownDescription: List archived repositories in the sidebar.

devspaces.includeForks.markdownDescription: List forked repositories in the sidebar.

devspaces.showOnlyDevspaces.markdownDescription: List only the repositories that have a devspace, whatever its state. **Show Only Devspaces** and **Show All Repositories** in the title bar of the view switch it.

devspaces.refreshIntervalMinutes.markdownDescription: Minutes between the background updates of the repository list from GitHub.

devspaces.hostAccessChecksOff.markdownDescription:
Repositories (`owner/name`) that may use the host of their Docker engine. Only for repositories you fully trust.

- Allows bind mounts, the Docker socket (control of every devspace), privileged mode, devices, GPUs, ports on all addresses
- The account checks stay on
- Or use **Turn Off Host Access Checks…** in the context menu of a repository

Example: `["majikmate/infra-tools"]`

anyOf.description: A regular expression (JavaScript syntax) for the repository name without the owner.

name.description: Name of a node that holds the groups of this regular expression. Without a name, its groups are shown directly under the owner.

pattern.description: A regular expression (JavaScript syntax) for the repository name without the owner.

flags.description: Flags of the regular expression: i (ignore case), u (Unicode), s (dot matches line breaks).

devspaces.repositoryGroups.markdownDescription:
Regular expressions on the repository name, without the owner, that filter the repositories of each owner in the sidebar and group them in levels. **[Edit Repository Groups…](command:devspaces.editRepositoryGroups)** opens an editor with a preview.

[Repository groups in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#repository-groups)

devspaces.confirmOpenFromLink.markdownDescription:
Ask before a link, for example on a website or a course page, creates a devspace of a repository of your account or of one of your organizations. **Always Open** in that question turns this off. A repository of another owner is always confirmed.

[Open from a link in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#open-from-a-link)

devspaces.vmMemoryGiB.markdownDescription:
The memory of the VM of Devspaces in GiB, from its next start. At most half of the memory of this computer: a larger value counts as that half, and Devspaces says so.

macOS and Linux only. On Windows, manage it via WSL.

[The VM of Devspaces in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#the-vm-of-devspaces-macos-and-linux)

devspaces.vmCpus.markdownDescription:
The CPUs of the VM of Devspaces, from its next start. At most half of the CPUs of this computer: a larger value counts as that half, and Devspaces says so.

macOS and Linux only. On Windows, manage it via WSL.

[The VM of Devspaces in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#the-vm-of-devspaces-macos-and-linux)

devspaces.createDockerContext.markdownDescription:
Create the Docker context `devspaces` for the VM of Devspaces, for other Docker tools. It never becomes the current context; turning this off removes it. It gives full access: manage devspaces only with Devspaces.

It works while the VM runs (macOS, Linux) or while a window of Devspaces is open (Windows).

[Other Docker tools in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#other-docker-tools)

devspaces.dockerHostsActions.markdownDescription:
The actions of the view Docker Hosts: Stop, Start, Remove… and Delete… of its objects, the actions of the hosts and of the VM of Devspaces, and the **+** that adds a remote host. In every mode, a click on an object opens its report, and **Refresh** and **Show Utilization** work.

[The view Docker Hosts in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#the-view-docker-hosts)
enumDescriptions: No actions: the view only shows the hosts and their objects.
The actions only in the context menu of a row (right-click), and the + in the menu … of the view.
The actions as buttons on each row and in its context menu, and the + in the title bar of the view.

devspaces.allowContainerLogs.markdownDescription:
Allow **Show Log** of every container in the view Docker Hosts: in the menu of each container row and on the report of a container, also of a container that is not of Devspaces, and **Show Log of the Monitor** on its reports. Off: no Show Log, and the Docker pipes of Devspaces refuse the log of every container.

[Report of a resource in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#report-of-a-resource)

devspaces.dockerHostsSettingsButton.markdownDescription:
Show the button **Docker Hosts Settings…** (a gear) in the title bar of the view Docker Hosts. It switches `#devspaces.dockerHostsActions#` and `#devspaces.allowContainerLogs#` in your user settings.

[The view Docker Hosts in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#the-view-docker-hosts)

devspaces.dockerHostsConsoleButton.markdownDescription:
Show the button **Open Console** (a terminal) on each host row of the view Docker Hosts. It opens a terminal with a shell on that host itself, not in a container: over SSH for a remote host, through `wsl.exe` for the WSL distribution of Devspaces, and over the SSH of Lima for its VM.

[The view Docker Hosts in the user guide](https://github.com/nimblescape/devspaces-vscode/blob/main/docs/guide.md#the-view-docker-hosts)
